title: Ulyana and the Thorn
premise: Vesper Amberdale keeps ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things until Ulyana, a child speaking a language older than kingdoms, arrives at his door carrying a thorn of living dragon-fire in her palm. The thorn is a fragment of the last dragon's heart, stolen by the thing that wears King Aldric's crown — a hollow wraith binding the king's body to its will. As guild hunters close in and the dragon-fire gutters toward extinction, Vesper must choose between loyalty to the guild that made him and the truth Ulyana carries. In the end he unbinds Aldric by returning the thorn through the king's own hand, at the cost of the guild's ledgers — and his place within them — while Ulyana, revealed as the dragon's final heir in human form, rekindles the fire.
about_author: Beatrix Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. She writes fantasy about people who keep records of impossible things.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: POV Vesper. A night of routine inventory at the Guild of Impossible Things establishes Vesper's meticulous world: bottled echoes, folded distances, debts written in candle-smoke. When a knock comes at midnight, he opens the door to find a mud-streaked child clutching something that burns without heat. Emotional beat: quiet order disrupted by wonder.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Vesper. Ulyana speaks words no guild translator can parse, yet Vesper recognizes fragments from a forbidden map fragment he once catalogued. The thorn in her palm pulses when she sleeps, showing him visions of a caged fire. Guild Master Corvane orders the child held for appraisal. Emotional beat: first loyalty test — obey or protect.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana, rendered in her broken new-tongue cadence. Through her eyes we learn the truth: she fled the capital, where the king's shadow moves wrong and guards with empty eyes hunt children born under comet-light. Her village burned for harboring her. Emotional beat: fear transformed into stubborn purpose.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Vesper. Corvane examines the thorn and declares it guild property, worth more than every ledger combined. Vesper falsifies an entry for the first time in his career, logging the thorn as 'depleted.' His mentor Sable notices the lie and says nothing — yet. Emotional beat: guilt braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Roads Not on Any Map
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Vesper and Ulyana flee using a folded-distance charm from inventory, stepping between unmapped places only a cartographer could navigate. Guild hunters led by Sable pursue. On the road, Ulyana teaches Vesper her language, and each word costs her strength. Emotional beat: fugitive tenderness; trust kindling.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV Vesper. They reach the capital disguised as map-sellers and witness the court: King Aldric, beautiful and vacant, signing decrees while the crown drinks the light around his head. Vesper realizes the wraith needs the thorn to complete its binding — the child walked into the trap willingly. Emotional beat: horror and dawning understanding of Ulyana's sacrifice.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Cornered by his former mentor, Vesper expects capture; instead Sable reveals she falsified ledgers once too — for a love the guild erased from its books. She gives them the palace's unmapped servant-paths but stays behind to hold the hunters. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into inheritance; the theme of loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Beneath the palace, in the old dragon-vault, they find the last dragon — vast, dying, its heart-hollow aching where the thorn was torn free. Ulyana confesses what she is: grown from the dragon's final ember to carry the thorn home. The wraith arrives wearing Aldric's body. Emotional beat: grief and awe; all secrets spent.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Vesper. Climax. The wraith offers Vesper everything the guild never gave him — permanence, importance, his name in every ledger — if he surrenders the thorn. Instead he uses cartographer's craft to fold the space between Ulyana and the dragon, letting her press the thorn into Aldric's own hand. The king's true self surges back and tears the crown-wraith apart. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered; love against duty resolved in action.

chapters.title: The New Cartography
chapters.summary: POV Vesper, epilogue-voiced. The dragon dies content, its fire passing into Ulyana, who remains a child with embers in her eyes. Aldric, freed but diminished, abolishes the comet-child hunts. Vesper begins a new ledger — not of possessions, but of truths owed and repaid — with Ulyana as his first entry. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; justice outside the law, gently kept.
